Arm-B's richer prose (the phone as 'weaponized summons,' the door as 'surrender rendered as a decision') is genuinely excellent on G and F, yet it introduces two self-inflicted faults arm-A avoids: it lets first-person quoted dialogue ('he knows what I know,' 'just another coppertop') leak into state fields that the register contract wants as external description (D=4), and it contains a load-bearing internal wobble where the phone's status change is 'cut dead mid-conversation' while Neo still says 'Yes' downstream, plus a mis-attributed evidence_scene (Neo's emotional exit cites sc-021 for a car-door beat grounded in sc-023) (A=4). Arm-A keeps the same interpretive reach while staying fully externalized and internally consistent, so on the dimensions a producer must defend at gate — A and D — it is the safer node. Both share the single upstream V5 ceiling (no named, costed degree-three theory-of-mind error), so that depresses them equally and does not break the tie.
